characters.name: open/close all folders
characters.description: Cheerful Child: All of them are generally happy-go-lucky babies, but it's taken to very extreme levels with Tommy Pickles, who is almost always upbeat. Fearless Infant: With the exception of Chuckie, all of them are babies who are seldom afraid of the harrowing and dangerous experiences they find themselves in. Malaproper: Given their young age, they often mispronounce words or think those words are something else. Prone to Tears: Despite them having a positive outlook on life, almost all of them cry fairly often, kind of justified since they are babies. Obviously, they started to cry much less inAll Grown Up!as they, of course, grew up.

characters.name: Tommy Pickles
characters.description: The main character and unofficial leader; he is best known for his incredible bravery and the screwdriver he always carries in his diaper. The Ace: He's viewed as such by his friends, being the one who usually makes the plans and takes the initiative to fix whatever problems the babies believe they're facing. Affectionate Nickname:Stu calls him "champ", implied later on to be a reference to Tommy living through his premature birth and growing up happy and healthy.Lou calls him "scout" when addressing him specifically, and calls the babies as a group "sprouts." Stu calls him "champ", implied later on to be a reference to Tommy living through his premature birth and growing up happy and healthy. Lou calls him "scout" when addressing him specifically, and calls the babies as a group "sprouts."

characters.name: Chuckie Finster
characters.description: In addition to his uncontrollable red hair, big glasses and bucked teeth, Chuckie is easily distinguished from his friends by his dislike of adventure and irrational fear of particular objects, most notably the "guy on the oatmeal box" (the Quaker Oats mascot). Afraid of Needles: In "The Shot", he says his experience with getting one was a horrific experience. He mentions having to be held down, which almost certainly didn't help. Anime Hair: His hair is what makes him recognizable. Art Evolution: Chuckie looks a bit different in Season 1, owing toEarly Installment Character-Design Difference. He has fewer strands on his hair, his nose has a slightly different shape, and his head shape is more boxy. His design was refined in Season 2. Badass Normal: An interesting variation. When one cartoon had the babies think Chuckie was a super hero to get back his inflatable globe from Angelica, he was told his cape was the source of his powers. He ends up losing the cape andstillbeating Angelica, knocking her over. He's shocked he did it, too.

characters.name: Phil and LilDeVille
characters.description: Half-Identical Twinswho are alike in every possible way, and even dressed to match. They represent the stage of infancy where babies are forever curious and try to eat and drink anything they can reach. Best known for their love of filth. Audience Surrogate: Phil was usually the one thinking what the audience was as well. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: For all their bickering, the two are as close as can be and miserable when one of them is separated. Baby Commercial Plot: They were once the stars of a diaper commercial in the episode "Baby Commercial". Due mostly to the director's attitude, the commercial was nearly a disaster and the twins' mother pulled them from it. When the director found out the finished product wasadoredby the client, he approached Mrs.DeVilleto get her to agree to more commercials.She turned him down cold. Big Eater: They love eating. They especially like mud, worms, and bugs.

characters.name: Angelica Pickles
characters.description: The eldest of the Rugrats, Angelica is theLarge Hamand bossy cousin of Tommy (their dads are brothers) and serves as the main antagonist of the series. She's a frequent bully to Tommy and the other "stupid babies" and when not dispensing incorrect wisdom, lives to make them miserable whenever they're in the same place. Being in the intermediate stage between infancy and early childhood, she is able to understand the babies' language and communicate with them. Age Lift: Downplayed inRugrats: A Live Adventure, where her bio in the musical's program booklet and the reprise of herVillain Song"Princess of the World" indicate that she is four years old, which means that she is one year older than her canonical age in the continuity of the stage musical. Anti-Role Model: She's pretty much the embodiment of what young childrenshouldn'tact like. Ate It All: Whenever she and the babies are given a plate of sweets to share with each other, she keeps all of them for herself and eats every last one.This has often resulted in her either getting a bad stomachache, scolded or punished by the adults, or both. Attention Whore: She gets enraged when people give more attention to the babies than to her.

characters.name: Susie Carmichael
characters.description: Susie moved across the street from Tommy early on in the series. A multi-talented, brave, and humble little girl, she served as the opposite of Angelica and often acted asThe Rivalto her. Like Angelica, she can understand the babies' language perfectly and communicate with them. The Ace: Downplayed and Justified. At a glance, she isWise Beyond Their Yearsand has many talents. But that's only because of a few factors.She's the oldest of the kids, and thus knows more, but she's just as prone to believing things that aren't true and mispronouncing words based on how the babies pronounce them.She has common sense, but she's still a kid, so she's able to be a part of the babies pretend games without much issue and tag along on their adventures without feeling out of place.Her mother is a career woman, and not only humble, but also has common sense - thus, Susie emulates her as a role model, tries and finds talent in things.She's the only main character with siblingsolderthan the others to observe, emulate, and ask questions of. She's the oldest of the kids, and thus knows more, but she's just as prone to believing things that aren't true and mispronouncing words based on how the babies pronounce them. She has common sense, but she's still a kid, so she's able to be a part of the babies pretend games without much issue and tag along on their adventures without feeling out of place. Her mother is a career woman, and not only humble, but also has common sense - thus, Susie emulates her as a role model, tries and finds talent in things.

characters.name: Dil Pickles
characters.description: Tommy's little brother, who was born inThe Movie. Unlike the others, he can't talk in full sentences, so he's a baby even to the other babies. As a newborn, most of his time is spent sitting around and drooling. Adapted Out:Despite the original production occurring well after the release ofThe Rugrats Movie, he isn't acknowledged at all inRugrats Magic Adventure(though this may have to do with the production being loosely adapted from the season two episode "Angelica the Magnificent", which aired long beforeThe Rugrats Moviewas released).He is absent in theBoom! StudiosRugratscomic book and the video gameRugrats: Adventures in Gamelandas a side effect of both being influenced primarily by the original series' pre-The Rugrats Movieera. Despite the original production occurring well after the release ofThe Rugrats Movie, he isn't acknowledged at all inRugrats Magic Adventure(though this may have to do with the production being loosely adapted from the season two episode "Angelica the Magnificent", which aired long beforeThe Rugrats Moviewas released). He is absent in theBoom! StudiosRugratscomic book and the video gameRugrats: Adventures in Gamelandas a side effect of both being influenced primarily by the original series' pre-The Rugrats Movieera. Annoying Younger Sibling: Tommy felt this way about him in the first movie, but now cares for him.

characters.name: Kimi Watanabe-Finster
characters.description: First appearing in the second movie, Kimi is an adventurous girl whose mother married Chuckie's father, making her his adopted sister. Adapted Out:While the first showing ofRugrats Magic Adventurepredates her debut movieRugrats in Parisby five months, no effort was made to incorporate her into the production for the remaining duration that the attraction was available. Like with Dil Pickles' absence, her omission even after her debut movie came out could be because the production was loosely based on "Angelica the Magnificent", an episode from the show's pre-The Rugrats Movieera.She doesn't appear in theBoom! StudiosRugratscomic book or in the video gameRugrats: Adventures in Gameland, since both are primarily influenced by how the original show was prior toThe Rugrats MovieandRugrats in Paris. While the first showing ofRugrats Magic Adventurepredates her debut movieRugrats in Parisby five months, no effort was made to incorporate her into the production for the remaining duration that the attraction was available. Like with Dil Pickles' absence, her omission even after her debut movie came out could be because the production was loosely based on "Angelica the Magnificent", an episode from the show's pre-The Rugrats Movieera. She doesn't appear in theBoom! StudiosRugratscomic book or in the video gameRugrats: Adventures in Gameland, since both are primarily influenced by how the original show was prior toThe Rugrats MovieandRugrats in Paris. Animal Lover: She likes all the animals she meets. She once threw away plastic toys to play with Fifi as she claims she likes real "aminals" better.

characters.name: Spike
characters.description: The Pickles family dog. He gets along very well with Tommy and often accompanies the babies on their adventures. Baby and Dog Bond: Tommy has a strong bond with him, perhaps best exemplified in "Spike Runs Away". Tommy gets upset when Spike runs away,every replacement pet Stu and Didi try is met with dead-ends, several flashback sequences show Tommy and Spike doing things that dogs do together, and Tommy is delighted when Spike is returned to his house by a rich man named Winston St. George. In turn, Spike is very protective of Tommy and on several occasions has saved him from dangerous animals, such as the mean bulldog in "Barbecue Story" and Scar Snout the Wolf inThe Rugrats Movie. Badass Adorable: He manages to beat up a wolf in the first film. Big Friendly Dog: Big compared to the babies, at least. Cartoon Dog Breed: He's an orange, noodle-eared dog withpurplespots. According to one episode of the original series, "Spike Runs Away", he's of the fictional "Siberian Tigerhound" breed.

characters.name: Belinda
characters.description: A toddler girl encountered by Tommy and Chuckie in the episode "Showdown at Teeter Totter Gulch". The Cameo: Her final appearance in the series is a cameo as one of Angelica's birthday party guests in "Angelica's Birthday". Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She is never seen again after her cameo in "Angelica's Birthday" (theRugrats Mystery AdventuresPC game notwithstanding) and is one of the most notable characters to not appear inAll Grown Up!. Food as Bribe:Rugrats Mystery Adventureswill have her be the informant for every case should the player choose to have Didi take the babies to the park and agree to recover Belinda's lost teddy bear, but she will only agree to help if you give her a Reptar bar twice (the first time to round up clues and the second time to determine which of the two suspects is the culprit). Lost Toy Grievance: Every visit to the park inRugrats Mystery Adventureswill have her upset that she's lost her teddy bear, with Tommy and friends having to get it back before she agrees to be an informant for the current case.

characters.name: Prudence/The Junk Food Kid
characters.description: A playground bully confronted by Tommy and Chuckie in "Showdown at Teeter Totter Gulch". The Cameo: She appears among Angelica's birthday party guests in "Angelica's Birthday", albeit with differently colored hair and clothes. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She's yet another character who only made a cameo after her debut episode and afterwards just disappeared. Defeat Means Friendship: She stops being a bully and becomes nicer after Tommy stands up to her. Laser-Guided Karma: At the end of the episode, she blows a giant bubble to get gum stuck to Tommy, but Tommy pops the bubble and it gets stuck to her face with her mother disappointed in herself for letting her have the gum.

characters.name: Dean
characters.description: A four-year-old Angelica has a crush on in "Angelica's in Love". Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Like with Belinda, his only other appearance after his debut episode is "Angelica's Birthday", the PC gameRugrats Mystery Adventuresis the only other media in the franchise he appears in and he is nowhere to be seen inAll Grown Up!. Food as Bribe: InRugrats Mystery Adventures, he is the informant whenever the player chooses to have Stu take the babies to the store. After beating him at hide and seek, and like when Belinda stipulates after her teddy bear is recovered, he will only help the player solve the case if he is given a Reptar bar twice. Nice Guy: He's a very amiable young boy.

characters.name: Jean-ClaudeDuMonte
characters.description: A French boy Angelica meets at the end of "Angelica's in Love". The Cameo: He appears among the guests at Angelica's birthday party in "Angelica's Birthday". Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: His only appearance after his debut episode is a cameo in "Angelica's Birthday", with the only other appearance he's made in the franchise overall being in the chapter bookBonjour, Babies. Everyone Looks Sexier if French: Angelica falls for him at first sight, particularly since she met him right after her falling out with her previous crush Dean. I Kiss Your Hand: He kisses Angelica's hand when they first meet.

characters.name: Harold Frumpkin
characters.description: A boy in Angelica and Susie's preschool class. He made a few appearances in the last season ofRugratsand has made several appearances in theAll Grown Up!spin-off. All Love Is Unrequited: Harold has a crush on Angelica, and may be the only guy out there who worships her the way she wishes everyone would. Unfortunately, Angelica treats him with disdain, as she does with the babies. Ascended Extra: InRugrats, Harold appeared in only three episodes. InAll Grown Up, he appeared in many episodes, sometimes acting asThe Sixth Rangerto the main characters. Blonde, Brunette, Redhead: A rare example involving both genders; he is the Redhead to Angelica's Blonde and Susie's Brunette. Minion with an F in Evil: In "Angelica's Assistant", Angelica hires him to be her assistant, which includes having him be mean to the babies so that she doesn't have to, as Charlotte threatened to take away her Cynthia dream yacht if she caught her doing so. Harold makes friends with the babies and can't bring himself to be mean to them.

characters.name: Taffy Maynston
characters.description: Lulu's teenage grandniece and lead singer of her own band. She is hired to become a regular babysitter for the babies later in the series. Affectionate Nickname: Calls the babies "Minis". Babysitter Friendship: Taffy is hired to look after the babies while Didi goesBack to Schoolto complete her master’s degree in child development. Taffy is a songwriter who has her own band, Taffy and the Saltwaters, and she has a soft spot for babies, whom she calls "Minis". The babies befriend her, and she takes them to wonderful places such as Boingo Burger, a fast food restaurant featured in "Hold the Pickles", and a video arcade featured in "Diapies and Dragons". Taffy even narrates the stories ofSnow WhiteandJack and the Beanstalkin the "Tales from the Crib" duology of direct-to-video movies. Cute Clumsy Girl: Tends to absentmindely knock things over when walking. Friend to All Children: The babies love her thanks to her being a kind-hearted babysitter who shares a strong bond with them.

characters.name: TimmyMcNulty
characters.description: The eldest of theMcNultybrothers, as well as their leader. He and his brothers have made a few appearances in the series. Alliterative Family: He and his brothers all have names that begin withT. His brothers' names areTerry,Ty,Todd, andTeddy. Believing Their Own Lies: He admits that he was lying about girls having "cooties," but when Lil, Angelica and Susie try to get back at him using bodypaint as their "cooties," he starts to believe its actually true after they "infect" Chuckie. Big Brother Instinct: Towards his younger brothers, when he believes Tommy popped Teddy's ball he tries to force him to apologize. "even to theMcNulty's not borned yet." The Bully: Likes to give Angelica and the babies a hard time on occasion.

characters.name: Larry and Steve
characters.description: A pair of slacker teenagers seen with a different job in every episode they appear in. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Barring background cameos, they are never seen again after Season 4's "Angelica Orders Out," and even in that episode, Steve is nowhere to be seen. The only other media in the franchise they've appeared in since are in the video gameRugrats: Studio Tour(where Larry is the tour guide for Giantamongus Studios and Steve is a security guard) and the stage musicalRugrats: A Live Adventure(where they appear as movers with aCanon Foreignernamed Astoria to perform the musical's first song "The Movers' Rap"). Fat and Skinny: Steve is the fat one, and Larry is the skinny one. New Job as the Plot Demands: They were ushers at the Octoplex theater in "At the Movies", stock clerks at Grocery World in "Incident in Aisle Seven", house painters in "Together at Last", Larry was a delivery boy for Zippy's in "Angelica Orders Out", and Larry was a tour guide while Steve was a security guard at Gigantomongous Studios in theStudio TourPS1video game. As mentioned in the description above, they never keep the same job for more than one episode. This could bejustifiedby the fact that they always mess up, causing them to get fired from all their jobs. Those Two Guys: They are usually seen together, though Larry appears independent of Steve in "Angelica Orders Out".

characters.name: Stu Pickles
characters.description: The father of Tommy and Dil, and husband of Didi. Also the younger brother of Drew and uncle of Angelica. A largely unsuccessfulBungling Inventorwith wacky ideas that occasionally come in handy. Art Evolution: Stu has a longer neck in the pilot. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: While most of the parents fall victim toParental Obliviousnessat times, Stu takes the cake. This is particularly prominent in "Toy Palace" (where he drags Chas to see some of the new toys in the store, giving Tommy and Chuckie the chance to explore) and "Turtle Recall" (where Chas trusts him to watch over the babies only for Stu to be distracted by a football game on TV). Berserk Button:Don't ever bad-mouth his inventions. This especially applies to his older brother, Drew.Don't ever tell Stu to get a real job. Stu claims that he would be wasting his life as "a clock-punching, paper-pushing, bean-counting accountant" (which is what Drew works as). Don't ever bad-mouth his inventions. This especially applies to his older brother, Drew.

characters.name: Didi Pickles
characters.description: Mother of Tommy and Dil, wife of Stu, and Angelica's aunt. A part-time schoolteacher who frequently consults a famous pediatrician for advice on how to raise the children. Accidental Misnaming:Aunt Miriam called her the following names — Dolly, Sally, Callie, Ginny, Phoebe and Fifi.And when the mothers go to a spa and get T-shirts with their names on them, Didi's reads 'Dodo' by mistake. Aunt Miriam called her the following names — Dolly, Sally, Callie, Ginny, Phoebe and Fifi. And when the mothers go to a spa and get T-shirts with their names on them, Didi's reads 'Dodo' by mistake. Anime Hair: Has very puffy hair.

characters.name: Grandpa Lou Pickles
characters.description: Father of Stu and Drew, and paternal grandfather of Tommy, Dil and Angelica. Being a grandparent and all, he is known for spoiling the babies at every opportunity and is generally considered by them to be their favorite of the grown-ups. Arc Number: 15 is often used in his stories. Blind Without 'Em: Can't see one bit if his glasses are lost (at one point this leads to a hilarious scene of him talking to Tommy's clown lamp - because he thought it was Didi!). Catchphrase:"In my day..." whenever he warms up another one of his stories."Fif-TEEN[so and so]!"His below mentionedCurse of The Ancientswhenever he's frustrated. "In my day..." whenever he warms up another one of his stories.

characters.name: Miriam Pickles
characters.description: Lou Pickles' cousin. Referred to as "Aunt Miriam" by Tommy, Angelica, and their parents despite technically being their cousin and not their aunt. Abhorrent Admirer: To Pirate Fred in "Club Fred". At the end of the episode, Miriam chases him on the beach. Captain Ersatz: of Martin's character Edith Prickley fromSCTV. Dirty Old Woman: She flirts with Pirate Fred in "Club Fred".Miriam:He's not much of a pirate, but Ilike his booty! The Dreaded: As a kid, she was this in the same vein as Angelica (being a bully who picked on everyone to cover up her insecurities). She's mostly just annoying as an adult, though the babies are shown to find her a tiny bit creepy every now and then.

characters.name: Lulu Pickles
characters.description: Lou Pickle's second wife and stepmother to Stu and Drew. Cool Old Lady: Quite a good dancer, and much younger in spirit than in age. December–December Romance: Both Lou and Lulu marry when they are elderly. Forgotten First Meeting: As mentioned above, Lou and Lulu were later revealed to have met when they were younger, only to move on and forget about it until now. The Ghost: Despite being mentioned several times, she's nowhere to be seen inAll Grown Up!. Apparently, she's travelling the world.

characters.name: Grandpa Boris Kropotkin
characters.description: Father of Didi, maternal grandfather of Tommy and Dil, and married to Grandma Minka. He is Ashkenazi Jewish, hails from "the old country" (implied to be Russia), and frequently laments abouthow much better things were therethan in America. He has a knack for storytelling and appears most prominently in the Hanukkah and Passover episodes displaying this talent. Black Bead Eyes: His eyes in all episodes up till the Passover special are drawn like black dots. Starting from the Channukah special, they look like regular eyes. The Bus Came Back: He comes back for some episodes ofAll Grown Up!. Cool Old Guy: Phil even lampshades this in one episode, describing him as something that is both cool and scary at the same time. Deadpan Snarker: Most infamously in "Home Movies" where he callsDr. Kevorkian(a prominent proponent of assisted suicide) because Stu's home movies are so boring.

characters.name: Grandma Minka Kropotkin
characters.description: Mother of Didi, maternal grandmother of Tommy and Dil, and married to Grandpa Boris. She displays many of the same stereotypical "Jewish grandparent" traits as her husband but is generally more mild-mannered and serves as thevoice of reasonfor him. The Bus Came Back: She turns up again for one episode ofAll Grown Up!. Funetik Aksent: Ditto to Boris. Funny Foreigner: Like Boris, she is Yiddish. I Was Quite a Looker: She finds her old dressmaker's dummy and muses about how slender she was in her youth. According to Boris, Minka was the most beautiful girl in the village that they lived in.

characters.name: Ben Kropotkin
characters.description: Half-brother of Didi, son of either Boris or Minka, maternal uncle of Tommy and Dil, and married to Elaine Kropotkin. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: After a cameo in "The Family Tree", he is never seen again and isn't even acknowledged inAll Grown Up!. Shout-Out: He and his wife Elaine are named after Benjamin Braddock and his love interest Elaine Robinson fromThe Graduate.

characters.name: Elaine Kropotkin
characters.description: Wife of Ben Kropotkin, sister-in-law of Stu and Didi and maternal aunt of Tommy and Dil. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: As with her husband, her last appearance in the show was a cameo in "The Family Tree" and she doesn't even get a mention inAll Grown Up!. Shout-Out: She and her husband Ben are named after Benjamin Braddock and his love interest Elaine Robinson fromThe Graduate.

characters.name: Drew Pickles
characters.description: Father of Angelica, uncle of Tommy and Dil, and married to Charlotte. The opposite of his younger brother Stu in almost every way, they do have their spats, but do care about each other. Aloof Big Brother: To Stu in their youth. While they have gotten closer as adults, he still can come off as hostile towards him at times. Their relationship likely would have been fine if Drew didn't insult him as often or was more supportive of his dream of inventing toys Belated Child Discipline: Drew struggles to discipline Angelica, due in part to being a workaholic parent who tends to give into her demands. However, as time goes on, he begins to punish her for her bad behavior. In "Runaway Angelica", he sends Angelica to her bedroom for playing in his office despite her having been repeatedly told not to, even going as far as not to fall for any of her "Sweet, apologetic child" tricks. In "Chuckie's Wonderful Life", she steals Chas' Latvian Folk dance CD and convinces Chuckie that it's his fault the CD got lost. When Drew finds out that Angelica stole the CD, he makes her apologize to Chas for taking it and forbids her from having dessert for a week. Big Brother Bully: SeveralNoodle Incidentaccounts have Stu perceive Drew as a very relentless case of this. Drew in turn regards Stu as anAnnoying Younger Sibling, while Lou's account implies Stu and Drew were both just as provocative as each other in childhood.Drew:Well, ifyouhadn't kicked my cash register then I wouldn't have thrown your rocket!Stu:Oh, yeah? Well ifyouhadn't made me play that dumb game—Lou:ZIP IT, THE BOTH OF YA! Corrupt Corporate Executive: His business practices are more shady and dishonest compared to his wife's.

characters.name: Charlotte Pickles
characters.description: Mother of Angelica, aunt of Tommy and Dil, and married to Drew. She's the CEO of her own company and is frequently seen talking on a cell phone toan invisible assistant(at least until "Mommy's Little Assets" and some later episodes where he was actually shown) named Jonathan. Action Dress Rip: In the third movie, complete withSexophone. The Beautiful Elite: She's wealthy (or of an upper status) and the most conventionally lovely of the adult female cast. Beauty, Brains, and Brawn: The Beauty to Didi's brains and Betty's brawn. Beauty Is Bad: She's the most conventionally physically attractive of all the women in the show but also has the least attractive personality (at least before herCharacter Development).

characters.name: Charles "Chas" Finster
characters.description: Chuckie's equally cowardly father. Was revealed to be a widower in the Mother's Day special episode, but got remarried in the second film,Rugrats in Paris. Acquired Situational Narcissism: When he becomes rich after winning a sweepstakes he becomes noticeably snobbish and arrogant, irritating Stu and Didi. Afraid of Blood: If hisFaintingat the sight of Tommy's bleeding finger in "The First Cut" is anything to go by. Ambiguously Jewish: Aside from acting similarly toWoody Allen, Chas says "Oy gevalt" in "Home Movies" and even his claim that "we're not really Jewish, actually we're not really anything" in "Passover" does not rule the possibility out. Art Evolution: During the first season, Chas' clothes had a different color and his hair was darker. However, this was changed during the second season.

characters.name: Kira Finster
characters.description: She is the mother of Kimi, adoptive mother to Chuckie, and Chas's second wife. Amicable Exes: Although the reasons for her divorce from Kimi's biological father Hiro Watanabe are never stated, it appears the two of them still maintain a good relationship.When he appears with his new wife and baby in "Trading Places" it's revealed her and Chaz were working with him to surprise Kimi with the visit and are helping him and his family find a place so he can be closer to Kimi. Berserk Button: It's not a good idea to try snatch a dress on sale that she saw first either. One lady during a baby sale at the mall learned this the hard way. Didi was also quite shocked. Beware the Nice Ones:She went nuclear when a woman tried to take a dress that Kira saw first.InRugrats in Parisshe stood up to Coco when she realized how much of a horrible person Coco was. She went nuclear when a woman tried to take a dress that Kira saw first.

characters.name: Melinda Finster
characters.description: Chas's deceased first wife and Chuckie's mother. Ambiguously Absent Parent: Before "Mother's Day", she was mentioned but never seen. One of the writers admitted that they weren't certain on whether she should be divorced or dead because theMoral Guardiansat Nickelodeon wouldn't allow for either topic on a show for as young a demographic as this one. Caring Gardener: Melinda enjoyed working in the garden and was a warm, loving wife and mother. Deceased Parents Are the Best: While Chuckie doesn't remember her that much, he does have fond memories of her in dreams when she played him and when he was around her wasn't afraid. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Before it was clarified that Chuckie's mother was deceased, the episode "Barbecue Story" features a background character who is possibly a prototype version of Melinda due to being seen next to Chas andlooking like a female version of him because she has red hair and glasses. Her depiction as shown in the "Mother's Day" episode, while still a redhead, is visibly distinct from her bereaved husband and son.

characters.name: HowardDeVille
characters.description: Father of Phil and Lil, and married to Betty. He is rather soft-spoken and little seen on the show compared to his wife but does make occasional appearances as a friend of the other babies' dads. Bumbling Dad: He is somewhat clumsy at times. Butt-Monkey: He is often prone to misfortune. Camp Straight: Looks effeminate, would like to be a movie director, and is married to Betty, who conversely can be considered Butch Straight. Childhood Friend Romance: He and Betty have been classmates as far back as the second grade. And back then she would poke him to get his attention as a way of expressing her crush. He eventually got it, and they've become a loving couple with two twin children.

characters.name: BettyDeVille
characters.description: Mother of Phil and Lil, and married to Howard. She is a very loud,athletic, and outgoing woman and clearly the more dominant partner in her marriage. Also usually portrayed as Didi's best friend. Beware the Nice Ones: She's a good natured, likable person unless youmess with her kids. Blonde, Brunette, Redhead: The Brunette to Charlotte's Blonde and Didi's Redhead. Brainy Brunette: Not an intellectual like Chas, Didi or Drew, but she's usually the voice of reason regarding blindly following the parental advice of experts by pointing out that said experts probably aren't that qualified and that she merely uses common sense when it comes to raising children. Bruiser with a Soft Center: She's a tough, rambunctious feminist who has a soft side, particularly for her kids.

characters.name: Lucy Carmichael
characters.description: Mother of Alisa, Buster, Edwin and Susie, and wife of Randy. A doctor and Harvard-educated wonder mom. The Ace: She is completely awesome at everything she turns her hand to: aviation, cooking, parenting, mechanical engineering, medicine. During the episode that introduces her and her husband, it's a running gag how Didi is constantly discovering new things to admire about her new friend and being totally blown away and a little intimidated. She's also quite friendly and kind — the kind of person who makes you wish you were cool enough to be her friend. Brainy Brunette: Has a head full of dark hair....and was a Harvard grad, currently works as a doctor, and took some courses from Le Cordon Bleu amongst other things. Doting Parent: Despite being a career woman, like Charlotte, she pays more attention to her kids and actually disciplines children if they don't behave properly. Good Parents: She cares about her daughter and always tries to cheer her up when she's upset.

characters.name: Randy Carmichael
characters.description: Susie's father and Buster and Edwin's uncle. Adaptational Early Appearance: Like his daughter, the original continuity had him debut in the second season episode "Meet the Carmichaels", while this continuity instead has him an established character from the very start. Adaptational Hairstyle Change: He has a flat top and is clean-shaven, when his original series counterpart had regular hair and a moustache (and was balding by the events ofAll Grown Up!). Adaptational Job Change: In the original series, Randy was the head writer forThe Dummi Bears. In this series, he's a high school science teacher. Adaptational Personality Change: Randy goes from being theOnly Sane Manof the fathers to Stu's fellowManchild.

characters.name: Alisa Carmichael
characters.description: Susie's 16-year-old sister, and the first-born daughter of the Carmichael family. Big Sister Instinct: Especially in "All Grown Up". In the episode "Susie Sings the Blues", while she is partially upset that the money she lent to Susie ended up being used in a scam, Alisa is more so angry/frightened of how much Susie put herself in danger, hanging around with an adult she didn't know, just because they claimed they could make her Pop Star dreams come true. Cool Big Sis: Despite feeling that her parents treat her like a little kid instead of a teenager and desiring more independence, she enjoys spending time with her younger siblings (especially Susie) and even enjoys reading children's books to her sister and to Tommy Pickles. Phoneaholic Teenager: She is rarely seen without her cell phone.

characters.name: Buster Carmichael
characters.description: Susie's eight-year-old brother, and the second-born son of the Carmichael family. Lovable Jock: He wears a red and white jersey and is often seen kicking his soccer ball. He is also admired by Susie and Edwin. The Prankster: In "The Last Babysitter", when Alisa is put in charge of babysitting him, he cuts the power and acts as if there is a monster in the house to get back at Alisa for making his friend Sticky go home. Tommy and Susie investigate and expose Sticky as the monster, foiling his plan. Sibling Rivalry: He has one with Alisa in "The Last Babysitter", as they butt heads for dominance.

characters.name: Edwin Carmichael
characters.description: Susie's six-year-old brother, and the third-born son of the Carmichael family. Bookshelf of Authority: When Susie introduces Tommy and Angelica to Edwin in "Tooth or Dare", Edwin is shown to sit at a desk with a large bookcase behind him, which Angelica mistakes for a library. Bookworm: When Susie, Tommy, and Angelica come to his bedroom to ask him about the Tooth Fairy in "Tooth or Dare", among the books in his collection is a copyThe Odysseyby Homer, and he is reading about quantum physics when they walk in. Child Prodigy: As the brains of the Carmichael family, his room is designed from the idea of a wealthy man's library, as he is an avid reader. Although he is the most quiet of the Carmichael siblings, he is extremely intelligent, as he is known for wearing Einstein pajamas, playing computer games, and he once built a laser with his friends at his birthday party. Smart People Wear Glasses: As part of his ensemble, he wears glasses with extremely large frames (bigger than Chuckie's).

characters.name: Dr. Lipschitz
characters.description: A world-renownedchild psychologist(who clearly has no idea what he's talking about) to whom Didi always quotes. Big Eater: He's more interested in the goulash dinner Didi is preparing than anything else, more interested in whether there are more eclairs than the fact that Didi is having a crisis, prepares himself a massive corned beef sandwich when left alone in the Pickles' house, and when prompted to say "cheese" while having his picture taken, immediately looks around for some. The Blind Leading the Blind: The man has NO idea what he's talking about, yet has a sizeable following of well-meaning parents plunging ahead blindly on his advice. Break the Haughty: He behaves like a self-important, arrogant know-it-all in "A Visit from Lipschitz" up until he's actually left alone with Tommy and Chuckie and realizes he has no idea how to stop their crying. Dumbass Has a Point: Despite being aKnow-Nothing Know-It-All, he does occasionally bring up good points. For example, inUnder Chuckie's Bed, Didi mentions that he says that a parent should talk to their child before changing their crib to a bed and considering that Chuckie didn't initially take well to the new bed, it's easy to see his point. Other solid pieces of advice include "ignore tantrums" and "it's not a big deal if your baby likes being naked."

characters.name: Jonathan
characters.description: Charlotte's frequently put-upon assistant. Audacity Earns Approval: When he found an embarrassing video of Charlotte and threatened to use it against her, rather than be angry she began to develop respect towards him. Butt-Monkey: Is constantly verbally abused by Charlotte. The Dog Bites Back: Downplayed in "Jonathan Babysits". Charlotte wants him to dig up dirt on the corporate competition while also making him babysit the kids in her place, a long fed up Jonathan decides to do dig up some dirt on Charlotte to teach her a lesson. When he presents an embarrassing home video of hernotean unkempt her in her bathrobe, face mask, and hair curlersto use against her, she's moreimpressed than angrybecause she realizes she underestimated him, and gives him a promotion. George Jetson Job Security: In "Mommy's Little Assets", Charlotte has Jonathan keep an eye on Tommy and Angelica when she is forced to take them to work due to all the adults being gone and no babysitter wanting to look after Angelica more than once. Jonathan neglects to keep an eye on the kids (which the all adults do at least once an episode), and Tommy and Angelica get away and roam the building. Charlotte immediately fires him after she finds the children, even going as far as to tell Jonathan to call security on himself. At the end of the episode, Charlotte re-hires Jonathan with a promotion as a reward for bringing Famous Ethel and Abe, who are impressed with her maternal instincts towards Angelica and have decided to sell their cookie company toMergeCorpbased on it, to her house. To Jonathan's dismay, it's not a Vice President position—it's supervisor ofMergeCorp'sdaycare center, starting with watching Angelica.Angelica:(grabs Jonathan's hand and smiles evilly) Boy, Jonathan, are we gonna have fun...

characters.name: Miss Carol
characters.description: The former host of the children's showMiss Carol's Happy House, whose undoing came when Angelica was to appear on it and overheard her swearing. Child Hater: Even though she's a kids' show host, she despises children. Depraved Kids' Show Host: Behind the scenes, she's a spiteful shrew who hates children and isn't above making profane statements about them.Miss Carol:Oh, you callthata fun phrase?! I'll tell you therealfun phrase. She thinks they're all little (car horn)! Nice Character, Mean Actor: She appears friendly and kindhearted on-camera, but off the clock is a surlyChild Haterwith no qualms about calling her target audience an obscenity. Role-Ending Misdemeanor:In-universe. Her admittance to insulting children by calling them an expletiveon airresults in her getting fired and her assistant Miss Stephanie taking her place.

characters.name: Rex Pester
characters.description: An obnoxious news reporter who will doanythingfor a story. Only appears inThe Rugrats Movie. Accidental Misnaming: He didn't even bother to get the children's names right, calling Tommy "Tammy", Dil "Dale", Phil and Lil "Bill and Jill", Chucky "Chunky" and Angelica "Amelia". The Antagonist: While Scar Snout is one to the babies, Rex is one to the parents due to being obnoxious and unsympathetic to their plight. Epic Fail: He not only gets all the kids' names wrong, he also misreports their pet as a horse. Hate Sink: He gets Drew to fight Stu and tells Didi that she might never see her children again. He's also not all that subtle about the fact that he doesn't really care about the lost babies he's pretending to be all heartbroken about and is exploiting the situation just to boost his own career.

characters.name: CocoLaBouche
characters.description: The primary antagonist ofRugrats in Paris, who tried to trick Chas into marrying her, so she could become president of Reptarland. Adapted Out: She does not appear in theRugratsnewspaper comic strip, since the arc introducing Kimi goes for aSlice of Lifeapproach and has nothing in common withRugrats in Parisaside from the babies visiting Paris and meeting Kimi there. Big Bad: She is the main antagonist ofRugrats in Paris. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Coco pretends to like kids in front of certain people like Kira, her boss, and Chas. Only the kids can see her true colors. In fact, Coco stops hiding her true colors as the movie progresses considering that she doesn't try to hide her hatred for the babies when they try to stop her wedding. Butt-Monkey: She does go through a couple of slapstick throughout the movie such as Dil attacking and throwing up on her. The most iconic one was when Angelica ripped her dress, exposing her underwear.It's well deserved, though.

characters.name: Jean Claude (Rugrats in Paris)
characters.description: Coco's lackey and the secondary antagonist. Adapted Out: He does not appear in theRugratsnewspaper comic strip, since the arc introducing Kimi goes for aSlice of Lifeapproach and has nothing in common withRugrats in Parisaside from the babies visiting Paris and meeting Kimi there. The Dragon: He serves as the main subordinate of Coco and assists her in her nefarious scheme. Final Boss: The console and PC versions of theRugrats in Parisvideo game both end with a boss fight against him controlling the Robosnail mecha. Humiliation Conga: Like his boss he's defeated in a very karmic yet very satisfying way considering that he gets his butt kicked by Tommy and his friends and ends up being chased out of the church by Spike after his boss's true colors have been exposed.

characters.name: Fluffy
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She acts like an innocent kitty most of the time, but takes delight in getting Spike into trouble. Cats Are Mean: What gets her on Spike's bad side. However, in "Babysitting Fuffy", she was mainly "mean" out of self-defense and was purring and being friendly when she's being doted on. This is further downplayed in later episodes where she is an aloof but otherwise friendly cat. A Day in the Limelight: Wasn't as prominent an animal character as Spike or the other dogs, being mostly limited to cameos or mentionings, though "Fluffy vs Spike", "Babysitting Fluffy" and the first half of "Be My Valentine" revolve around her. Early-Bird Cameo: Cameos in "Touchdown Tommy" before being properly introduced in "Fluffy vs. Spike" shortly after. Female Feline, Male Mutt: Female Feline to Spike's Male Mutt.

characters.name: Fifi
characters.description: The Finsters' poodle, adopted inRugrats in Paris. Babies Ever After: She and Spike had puppies in "Bow Wow Wedding Vows". Big Friendly Dog: She's just as nice to the babies as Spike. Love at First Sight: With Spike. Love Interest: To Spike, and they get together too.

characters.name: Spiffy
characters.description: Keet: Highly hyper and playful. Meaningful Name: He is called "Spiffy" as he is the son of Spike and Fifi. Troublemaking New Pet: He is rambunctious and hard to train.

characters.name: Pepper
characters.description: Beware the Quiet Ones: She's timid and shy, but when she sees Angelica intimidating Chuckie, she gets in front and starts barking at Angelica until the latter backs away. Genki Girl: She was named "Pepper" because of her peppy personality. Meaningful Name: Was named Pepper due to her pep. Shrinking Violet: Early on, as she was very shy and would hide from everyone. Sibling Yin-Yang: She's not nearly as rambunctious as her brother, Spiffy.

characters.name: Scar Snout
characters.description: Adapted Out: Due to Dil's introductory arc taking more of aSlice of Lifeapproach with none of the babies in real peril, he does not appear in theRugratsnewspaper comic strip. Disney Villain Death:During the movie's climax, he is pulled off the bridge by Spike and falls into the river. The Dreaded: He is feared by all the animals in the forest. In fact, the moment he shows up in the climax, the circus monkeys flee in fear at the sight of him. Knight of Cerebus: Scar Snout brings a noticeably more tense atmosphere and would've killed the babies had Spike not been around. He is also the onlyRugratsantagonist that is seeminglyKilled Off for Real. Vile Villain, Saccharine Show: He's aSavage Wolfplayed straight in a kid's movie, and the darkest threat the babies ever faced.

characters.name: Reptar
characters.description: A JapaneseKaijufrom a film franchise the babies love. Breakout Character: Became very popular and had quite a few episodes to himself as time went on. AfterThe '90s Are All Thatwas rebranded asThe Splat, Reptar was the subject of everyRugratsrelated advertisement. He even becomes the Rugrats rep forNickelodeon All-Star Brawl. Breath Weapon: Reptar can breathe fire. Bully Hunter: Reallyhatesaliens showing uptrying to take over and boss mankind around. Catchphrase: "Halt! I am Reptar!", though later on he becameThe Voiceless.

characters.name: Dactar
characters.description: All Flyers Are Birds: Being babies, Phil and Lil don't quite seem to get what Dactar is. Phil thinks he's a giant bird, Lil thinks he's a butterfly. They're both wrong, but Phil's guess is a little closer. Big Bad Duumvirate: Originally shared this role in the movie with the false Reptar, and possibly theMad Scientist. Decoy Antagonist: OfRunaway Reptar. Turns out therealvillain is Reptar's robot replica and its creator. Expy: The Rodan to Reptar's Godzilla. Giant Flyer: As a pterodactyl based kaiju, this is a no brainer.

characters.name: Robo-snail
characters.description: It is a giant purple snail cyborg with pincer-tipped claws and tank tread feet attached to its shell. Cyborg: It's a giant snail with built in limbs and weaponry. Expy: As a robotic arch-enemy to Reptar, it draws parallels with Mecha-Godzilla, though in the film proper, it ironically looks more organic than the protagonists own mecha based on its rival. Foreshadowing: First appears as a toy that Phil and Lil play with aboard the plane on the way to Paris (which the stewardess steps on), then again in the storage area where the robots are. Fast forward to the climax where Jean-Claude hijacks its giant robot to chase down and fight the babies (who have control over Reptar's robot). Human Hammer-Throw: The giant robot version piloted by Jean-Claude does this —Bowser style— the the babies' Reptar mech while singing to the tune ofLa Donna É Mobile.

characters.name: Cynthia
characters.description: The Ace: There are Cynthia dolls with just about every profession imaginable. Justified, because she's aBarbieparody. Allegorical Character: While "character" may be stretching it, Cynthia is basically "that" toy. The ones (typically dolls or action figures) that have been messed up by more hands-on children who'd curiously prod and stress-test them by pulling out hair, removing clothes, drawing on them etc. Despite them possibly looking rough or creepy afterwards, said toys tend to be beloved by their kids (at least for a time) and might become a source of fond memories. Butt-Monkey: She tends to get messed up pretty badly, usually asLaser-Guided Karmafor Angelica, though sometimes Angelica herself is the one doling out the doll's abuse. Lampshaded in one episode, wherein Angelica mentions that Cynthia's "been through a lot lately". Companion Cube: Angelica carries her around and acts as if she's a living person. Creepy Doll: To a slight degree. Granted, the creepiest thing about her is that she'sAngelica'sfavorite toy, though her overall unnerving appearance doesn't help much.

characters.name: The Dummi Bears
characters.description: Beary Friendly: Being a parody of theCare Bears, they don't have any mean bones in their bodies. Expy: Of theCare Bears. Leitmotif: "SING A HAPPY HAPPY HAPPY HAPPY HAPPY HAPPY SONG!" The Movie: "At the Movies" is set around the Pickles going to the multiplex and the adults watchingThe Dummi Bears in The Land Without Smiles.Grandpa Lou:Land Without Brains is more like it! The Pollyanna: All of them are very optimistic.

characters.name: Goober the Gopher
characters.description: Alliterative Name:Goober theGopher. Catchphrase: "Can I have a hug?" Friend to All Children: Goober is a friendly gopher who loves to give hugs to children. Unfortunately, Tommy dislikes him because Goober doesn't want to do anything other than give hugs. Kids' Show Mascot Parody: Goober is an obvious parody ofBarney the Dinosaur, as he speaks in a goofy voice, loves hugs, and lacks any emotion other than happiness. In his second appearance in "No Place Like Home", he is colored purple with with green hair, which is also the color palette of Barney.

characters.name: Dr. Spooky
characters.description: Ascended Extra: In the original "All Growed Up" special, he's merely a character in a TV show the Rugrats were watching in the beginning before they got the idea to build their own time machine and use it to time-travel a decade into the future. In the PC game adaptationRugrats: All Growed Up, he has a much larger role, as his own time travel experiment causes the Rugrats to go forward in time and age by ten years (in addition to apparentlygetting stuck in his show's universe) and the children have to help him build an un-time machine so he can reverse the process and send them home in their normal ages. Einstein Hair: Like your typical mad scientist, his hair is wild and gray. Large Ham: As expected of mad scientists and characters voiced by Charlie Adler, he's very loud and melodramatic. Mad Scientist: He's a demented scientist who creates a time machine powered by a pumpkin and uses his assistant Todd as an unwilling guinea pig. Smart People Wear Glasses: He's a bespectacled mad scientist.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Cheerful Child: All of them are generally happy-go-lucky babies, but it's taken to very extreme levels with Tommy Pickles, who is almost always upbeat. Fearless Infant: With the exception of Chuckie, all of them are babies who are seldom afraid of the harrowing and dangerous experiences they find themselves in. Malaproper: Given their young age, they often mispronounce words or think those words are something else. Prone to Tears: Despite them having a positive outlook on life, almost all of them cry fairly often, kind of justified since they are babies. Obviously, they started to cry much less inAll Grown Up!as they, of course, grew up.

characters.name: Kimi Watanabe
characters.description: Adaptational Backstory Change: In the 1991 series, the babies first met her atthe EuroReptarland theme park in Paris, France. In this series, she and Kira moved to Tommy's neighborhood from Paris, and the babies first meet her at Angelica's preschool. Adaptational Early Appearance: This version of her debuts in the first half of the first season's 12th episode and appears before Dil Pickles is born, when her original series counterpart didn't appear until after Dil Pickles' introduction inThe Rugrats Movieand made her debut inRugrats in Paris, which came out between the original series' sixth and seventh seasons. In addition, she debuts twelve episodes/segments before her mother Kira appears, when both characters in the original continuity debuted together in theRugrats in Parismovie. Age Lift: Reimagined to be three years old in the series, essentially reversing ages with Susie. Companion Cube: In "The Heist", she has a stuffed ferret named Freddy. When Freddy gets put up for auction, she begs for Angelica to help her get him back. Girlish Pigtails: Retains her three pigtails from the original series.

characters.name: Josh
characters.description: Adaptational Early Appearance: His sole appearance in the original cartoon was in the third season episode "New Kid in Town", while this continuity has him debut in the first season episode "The Two Angelicas". Adaptational Slimness: In the 1991 series, Josh was a fat kid. In this series, he's thinner. Ascended Extra: In the 1991 series, Josh was aOne-Shot Characterwho only appeared in "New Kid in Town". In this series, he makes recurring appearances as one of Angelica's preschool classmates. Composite Character: His recurring role, thinner appearance and more overt antagonism towards the other children make him more reminiscent of TimmyMcNulty. Hero with an F in Good: He proves to be this in "The Favor". When Susie pulls his stick out of the tree, he decides to repay her by doing her a favor. However, his acts of kindness aren't what Susie had in mind. When she wants him to get her a juice box, he takes one from another girl. When Susie wants him to hold her placein line at the slide, he cuts in line. When Susie tries unsuccessfully to teach him how to be nice, things get worse from there. He picks flowers to give to the girl whom he took the juice box from, only for a bee to fly out of the flowers and chase her away, and when a boydrops his ice cream, he scoops it back up for him rather than give him a new one. In the end, Josh puts his stick back in the tree so that he doesn't have to do any more favors for anyone, since trying to being nice was was too much work for him.

characters.name: Begley Snodgrass
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: He never appears in the original series. In Touch with His Feminine Side: He's a boy who wears a pink jacket and collects dolls. Lost Toy Grievance: In "Ancient Treasure", he laments the loss of his Juniper doll, a toy from his babyhood that was the only Cynthia merchandise he actually played with instead of keeping in its original packaging to preserve its collector's value. He takes it pretty hard in the episode's imagination sequence when he's forced to give up a chance to replace his lost Juniper doll with Angelica's (which she doesn't have nearly as much sentimental attachment towards). Vitriolic Best Buds: He and Angelica are best friends, but she finds him annoying due to his preferring to collect dolls than play with him.

characters.name: Barry and Eve
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: They don't appear in the original series. No Full Name Given: We don't know their surnames. Phoneaholic Teenager: They both appear to be in their late teens, and are commonly seen on their cell phones. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: Since they're a pair of teenagers seen working various jobs and even have names that rhyme with those of their predecessors, they're essentially replacements for Larry and Steve from the original series, though Barry resembles Steve more than Larry and Eve looks more like Larry than Steve, plus Eve is female and black.

characters.name: Gabi
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: She doesn't appear in the original series. Genki Girl: She's shown to be lively and playful when babysitting her baby cousins and their friends. No Full Name Given: Her last name is unspoken.

characters.name: Nina
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: She never makes an appearance in the original series. Companion Cube: She treats her wrench like a toy and calls it Wanda. No Full Name Given: We don't know her last name. Wrench Wench: She's always carrying around a wrench.

characters.name: Simon
characters.description: Julian's son, Judith's stepson, Charlotte's stepbrother, Drew's stepbrother-in-law and Angelica's stepuncle. Bratty Half-Pint: He's a very malicious child who enjoys causing trouble. Canon Foreigner: Like his father, he did not exist in the original 1991 series and is exclusive to the 2021 reboot. Evil Brit: He's British and very cruel. Eyes Out of Sight: One of his eyes is obscured by his hair.

characters.name: Lou Pickles
characters.description: Angelica, Tommy, and Dil's grandfather and Drew and Stu's father. Adaptational Hairstyle Change: His hair is the same as it was in the original series except he now has a ponytail. Adaptational Personality Change: Due to the shifted timeline, Lou goes from being aGrumpy Old Manmilitary veteran to a calmNew-Age Retro Hippie.noteLou was apparently born in 1915 in the original series, and since the reboot is supposed to be set thirty years later than the original, Lou would've been born in 1945. Since the average hippie was fifteen to twenty-five years old, Lou would've been old enough to actually be a part of the hippie movement. Friendship Song: "The Pickle Barrel" ends with him and his old friend and musical partner Bob Brine proving their reconciliation by singing "I've Got Your Back". New-Age Retro Hippie: Lou takes on this persona in the series, right down to wearing tie-die and practicing yoga.

characters.name: Chas Finster
characters.description: Adaptational Backstory Change: In the original series, he and Kira first met each other atthe EuroReptarland theme park in Paris, France. In this series, Kira and Kimi move to Tommy's neighborhood from Paris, and Chas first meets Kira at Angelica and Kimi's preschool carnival in "Lucky Smudge". Adaptational Job Change: In the original series, Chas was largely a bureaucrat, but owned and operated the Java Lava coffee house in the last few seasons. In this series, he appears to be a music teacher, as he mentions giving piccilo lessons in "I, Baby" and gives piano lessons in "Lucky Smudge". Disabled in the Adaptation: While in the original series, he was nearsighted, asthmatic, and allergic to cats, here, he's also lactose intolerant, as revealed in "Little Daddy". Plot Allergy: "Little Daddy" reveals him to be lactose intolerant. Wedding Finale:The final episode "Big Cake Day" ends with him marrying Kira.

characters.name: Trish Lavone
characters.description: BettyDeVille's girlfriend. Canon Foreigner: She's clearly another character exclusive to the 2021 series who didn't exist in the original 1991 cartoon, since Betty in that continuity was straight and married to a man named Howard. Nice Girl: She's very approachable and wants to be on good terms with everyone. Satellite Love Interest: There isn't much to her other than being Betty's life partner.

characters.name: Howard Tucker
characters.description: Phil and Lil's biological father and college friend of BettyDeVille. Adaptational Late Appearance: HowardDeVillein the original continuity first appeared with his wife Betty in the series premiere "Tommy's First Birthday" (or the unaired pilot short "Tommy and the Great White Thing" if you count the prototype versions of Phil and Lil's parents), while this continuity waits until the third season episode "Desert Trip" to properly introduce him. Adaptational Romance Downgrade: He was BettyDeVille's husband in the original 1991 cartoon, but, while still being Phil and Lil's father, is instead a close friend of the twins' mother. Adaptation Name Change: Due to not being married to Betty in this continuity, his surname is now Tucker instead ofDeVille. Demoted to Extra: In contrast to being a recurring character in the original show, this version of Howard only gets a full appearance in one episode.

characters.name: Kira Watanabe
characters.description: Adaptational Backstory Change: In the original series, she and Chas first met each other atthe EuroReptarland theme park in Paris, France. In this series, she and Kimi moved to Tommy's neighborhood from Paris, and she and Chas first meet each other at Angelica and Kimi's school carnival in "Lucky Smudge". Adaptational Early Appearance: While first appearingseveral episodes after her daughter's introduction, she still appears earlier in this continuity than her 1991 series counterpart due to debuting in "Lucky Smudge", the first half of the first season's 19th episode, when the original continuity had her first appear in the movieRugrats in Paris, which was released between the original cartoon's sixth and seventh seasons. Like her daughter, she is also introduced in this continuity before Dil Pickles is born when the original continuity didn't introduce them until after Dil was added to the cast. Adaptational Job Change: In the last few seasons of the 1991 series, Kira worked alongside Chas at the Java Lava coffee shop. In this series, she works as a librarian. Adaptational Late Appearance: While a case ofAdaptational Early Appearancein that she debuts in the first season of the 2021 series and prior to Dil Pickles' birth in contrast to her original series counterpart debuting after Dil Pickles' introduction in a movie that was released between the original cartoon's sixth and seventh seasons, she also qualifies as appearing later than her original counterpart due to her daughter debuting in "Escape from Preschool" before she appears, when she and her daughter both debuted in theRugrats in Parismovie in the original continuity. Wedding Finale:The final episode "Big Cake Day" ends with her finally marrying Chas.

characters.name: Boris Kropotkin
characters.description: Didi's father and Tommy and Dil's maternal grandfather. Adaptational Late Appearance: He and Minka debut in "The Bubbe and Zayde Show", the first half of the first season's ninth episode, when the original show had them debut in the first season's first episode "Tommy's First Birthday". Adaptational Nice Guy: He's less of a sardonic grump and is on better terms with Lou than he was in the original 1991 cartoon. Doting Grandparent: He and his wife enjoy using facetime to entertain their grandson Tommy by using sock puppets and pretending they're different characters. You Don't Look Like You: He's been drastically redesigned to appease complaints that his original appearance came off as an antisemitic caricature, particularly being skinnier and having a less sizeable nose. About the only trait he retains from his original design is being bald.

characters.name: Minka Kropotkin
characters.description: Didi's mother and Tommy and Dil's maternal grandmother. Adaptational Late Appearance: While the original series had her and Boris debut as early as the premiere episode "Tommy's First Birthday", this continuity waits until "The Bubbe and Zayde Show", the first half of the first season's ninth episode, to introduce them. Doting Grandparent: She and her husband enjoy putting on puppet shows through facetime to entertain their grandson Tommy. You Don't Look Like You: Like her husband, she was drastically redesigned for the reboot to appease complaints that her original appearance looked like an antisemitic caricature. She actually looks more like Grandpa Lou's cousin Miriam from the original show.

characters.name: Judith
characters.description: Charlotte's mother, Drew's mother-in-law and Angelica's grandmother. Adaptational Onscreen Appearance: She makes a physical appearance here, when the original series only mentioned Angelica's grandmother in "Angelica's Birthday", where Drew reads Angelica a birthday card from her (and could only have been Angelica's maternal grandmother, since it's established that Stu and Drew's mother Trixie is deceased and likely passed away before Angelica and Tommy were born). May–December Romance: Her current husband is her son-in-law Drew's age (and strongly resembles him as well). Mum Looks Like a Sister: Even forces Charlotte to tell everyone including Angelica that she is Charlotte's sister and not her mother. Named by the Adaptation: She is named Judith, when her name was never revealed in the original series due to only being indirectly mentioned once.

characters.name: Julian
characters.description: Judith's current husband and Charlotte's stepfather. Canon Foreigner: He is a new character exclusive to the 2021 series who did not exist in the original 1991 series or any of its related media. May–December Romance: He's as old as Drew and is married to Drew's mother-in-law, who is significantly older.

characters.name: Daxton
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: He often is subject to comedic injuries while making deliveries. Canon Foreigner: He never appears in the original series. No Full Name Given: We don't know his last name. Spell My Name with a "The": His food critic name is the Invisible Eater.

characters.name: Celeste
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: She doesn't appear in the original series, since there, Lou had a different girlfriend (and later wife) Lulu. December–December Romance: She's an old lady, and she begins dating Grandpa Lou in "Captain Susie". Friend to All Children: She's friendly with the kids, bonding with Angelica over Cynthia dolls and encouraging her to give Chuckie his Reptar doll. No Full Name Given: Her last name is unstated.

characters.name: Bob Brine
characters.description: An old friend and musical partner of Lou Pickles who had a falling out with him for years, but eventually reconciles with him. Alliterative Name: His given name and surname both begin with the letter B. Canon Foreigner: Is yet another character exclusive to the 2021 series who did not exist in the continuity of the original 1991 cartoon. Friendship Song: When he and Lou renew their friendship at the end of "The Pickle Barrel", they sing a song called "I've Got Your Back".

characters.name: Graham Prescott
characters.description: Ambiguously Bi: He's hinted to be attracted to men in his debut episode, but "Traditions" has him engage in flirtatious conversation with Betty's Tia Esperanza. Canon Foreigner: He doesn't appear in the original series. Incompatible Orientation: He initially wanted to date Lou due to Angelica using his dating app without really knowing what she was doing, but since Lou doesn't like men in that way, they eventually ended up making friends instead. Mall Santa: He is shown working as a mall Santa at the beginning of "Traditions". New-Age Retro Hippie: He's a hippie like Lou, having braided hair and colourful clothes.
